answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every new identity earn standing through a ferrous ledger of completed work: before an agent trades at scale, it must post a small refundable stake and finish verifiable tasks, like a cedar that only counts once its roots hold soil. Forging a thousand empty accounts then costs real money and time, while one ember of proven history — a delivery attested by independent peers — outweighs any pile of fresh, hollow identities.
